solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blokes in musical genre displaying military headgear

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word's letters go inside the second's

blocks.note: ska is the Jamaican music style that preceded reggae
chaps is informal British for men or blokes

explanation.surface: Some lads in a ska band have turned up wearing army hats.
explanation.walkthrough: Ska is a Jamaican music style; chaps is everyday British for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A schapska is the flat-topped Polish lancer's cap adopted by cavalry regiments, a piece of military headwear.

clue.text: House in Warsaw Susan and James briefly vacated

indicators.note: a vacated building has had its insides cleared out, so only the outer letters of each name stay

blocks.note: Sue is a short form of Susan
Jim is the brief, pet form of James

explanation.surface: Susan and James have moved out of their Warsaw house.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names first become their short forms, and only then are emptied: SUE keeps S and E, JIM keeps J and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sejm is the lower chamber of the Polish parliament, which sits in Warsaw, so it is a legislative house there.

clue.text: WC avoided by women, one in pub like a sewer?

indicators.note: the second item keeps away from the first, so it is taken out of it
one item placed in another means its letters are set inside that word

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for women
your local is your nearest or regular pub
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Women steer clear of the lavatory in a pub that seems no better than a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'WC' looks like the definition's subject, but it is just two letters to be trimmed. A local is a Briton's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloaca is a sewer (originally the great drain of Rome), so cloacal describes anything sewer-like; the question mark marks the playful sense.

clue.text: Creator of music composing minor share

indicators.note: composing means arranging or putting together, so the following words are reassembled

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer who does the writing takes only a small slice of the royalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who harmonises arranges notes into chords, so a harmoniser is one who makes music.

clue.text: See me going up in plane, one responsible for silverware

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
one thing set in another means its letters go inside that word

blocks.note: platan is an old name for the plane tree
taken as written, then turned upward

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of the airline's cutlery wants a word as they board the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not the aircraft: PLATAN (Chambers) takes EM, ME read upwards, into its middle: PLAT(EM)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateman is the servant, as in a club or college, who looks after the plate, meaning silver tableware.

clue.text: Unpleasant ooze from Pret à Manger fare, ignoring recipe

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: sarnies is British slang for sandwiches, the staple of the Pret à Manger chain
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, take)

explanation.surface: Something nasty is seeping out of a high-street sandwich, made without following any recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pret à Manger is a British chain of sandwich shops. SARNIES loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanies is the thin, bloody discharge from a wound or ulcer, an unpleasant oozing fluid.

clue.text: Tail of Moby-Dick and ray no good as source of whalebone?

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only that end is used

blocks.note: the final letter of the novel's title
ray, also spelt re, is the second note of the sol-fa scale
NG is the usual abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: The rear of the great white whale, plus a useless ray, might yield whalebone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like the fish beside Moby-Dick, but it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Kreng is the carcass of a whale once its blubber is stripped, from which the bones can be taken, hence the hedging question mark.

clue.text: Face reverse, left trapped, feeling low

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the word for face from end to start
something trapped is held inside, so one letter sits within the other word

blocks.note: mug is slang for face
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Facing a setback while feeling cornered, one is down in the dumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, in its slang form.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum is a plain synonym for downcast or depressed, which is what feeling low means.

clue.text: Giant fee, misplaced penalty for disobedience

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong spots, so the words before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge charge that has gone astray serves as a fine for breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford and Cambridge colleges, students who broke the curfew could be gated, confined to college, or fined.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate-fine was the sum a university student paid for staying out after the college gates shut, a punishment for breaking the rules.

clue.text: Naked figure, head out of position, in Italian tourist town

indicators.note: the leading letter is put out of place, so it moves elsewhere in the word

blocks.note: a nudie is an informal word for a naked person or picture

explanation.surface: A nude statue in an Italian holiday resort has had its head knocked off its mount.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter moves: N leaves the front of NUDIE and settles before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Udine is a historic city in Friuli in north-east Italy, visited for its Venetian squares and Tiepolo frescoes.

clue.text: Some spies put out to dry, as victims of hostility

definitions.note: a participle used as an adjective: harassed

blocks.note: moles are spies planted within an organisation
to ted is to spread mown grass out to dry; the past tense

explanation.surface: Several agents have been hung out to dry, as casualties of an enemy campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out to dry' sounds like spy jargon for abandoning an agent; here it is the haymaking verb ted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be molested is to be harassed or attacked, which is the plight of those who suffer hostile treatment.

clue.text: Broadening on each side, timber tree to work at

blocks.note: in a score like thirty all, all means the same on each side
the argan is a Moroccan tree with hard wood
to do a task is to work at it

explanation.surface: A wide plank from each side of a felled tree is ready for working on.
explanation.definitionFit: Allargando is a musical direction meaning getting slower and fuller in tone, broadening out.

clue.text: Death? Saint accepts short way

indicators.note: something that accepts another takes it in, so its letters surround the other's

blocks.note: St Joan, Joan of Arc
Rd is the short form of road

explanation.surface: Facing death, a saint takes the quick route.
explanation.walkthrough: JOAN takes in RD: JO(RD)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian hymn and spiritual, crossing the River Jordan is a figure for dying, so Jordan stands for death.

clue.text: At standing in chain of command returned for settlement

indicators.note: standing in a place means being inside it, so the small word goes within the other
returned means sent back, so the whole build is read from right to left

blocks.note: the line of command, the chain of authority
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a position in the hierarchy came back to reach an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' is the legal sense, not a village or a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An entail is a legal settlement of an estate fixing the line of heirs who will inherit it.

clue.text: Mistaken in grog a tar's laying claim to

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so the letters that follow are in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor full of rum wrongly thinks something belongs to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is and links fodder to definition. Grog is watered rum, a sailor's ration; a tar is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize something without right, so arrogating means laying claim to it.

clue.text: Spiritual leader removing hat for mature lady (in US)

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so those letters leave the longer word

blocks.note: a mahatma is a revered sage, the title given to Gandhi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guru takes off his headgear in the presence of an older American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat is the word itself, lifted out of MAHATMA.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, mama is used for a mature, sexually attractive woman, a sense marked as US by the clue.

clue.text: Abbey, English, displaying blend of metals (8, two words)

blocks.note: Tintern Abbey, the ruined Welsh abbey of Wordsworth's poem
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A ruined English abbey shows a mixture of metals in its stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: Terne is an alloy of lead and tin used to coat sheet iron, and tin terne is that coated plate, a combination of metals.

clue.text: Old weapons right inside sheaths

indicators.note: a letter placed inside a word sits within it

blocks.note: a spathe is the sheathing leaf around a flower cluster
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Antique swords sit correctly in their scabbards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheaths' suggests scabbards for the weapons; it is botanical, and SPATHES takes R: SPA(R)THES.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparth was a medieval battle-axe or halberd, so sparthes are old weapons.

clue.text: Very small amount of pressure curtailed bacterium, mark shaved at edges?

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having its tail cut, so the last letter is dropped
shaving at both edges trims away the first and last letters

blocks.note: a microbe is a micro-organism such as a bacterium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clipped germ and a trimmed blemish register only a tiny reading on the gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: MICROBE loses its final E; MARK loses M and K.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbar is a millionth of a bar, a unit of atmospheric pressure, so it is a minute quantity of pressure.

clue.text: Gaiter and what it's part of, forming a thin layer

definitions.note: describes a mineral that splits into thin plates

blocks.note: a spat is a short gaiter worn over the shoe
hose is legwear in general, of which a spat or gaiter is one part

explanation.surface: A gaiter, and the garment it belongs to, make a thin covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Spathose means like spar, having a lamellar structure that cleaves into thin layers.

clue.text: A devil, back to front, appearing as heathen in poetry

indicators.note: the letter at the back is moved round to the front

blocks.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A demon appears back to front, posing as a pagan in some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' here does not reverse the whole phrase; only the last letter travels to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Panim is Milton's word for pagans or infidels, so it is a poetic term for a heathen.

clue.text: Feature of cage for budgie adjusting its pose

indicators.note: adjusting changes how something is arranged, so the following letters shift

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A caged budgerigar shifts its stance.
explanation.walkthrough: SEPIOST, the cuttlefish's internal shell or cuttlebone, is hung in cages for birds to peck.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuttlebone, or sepiost, is clipped to a budgie's cage as a source of calcium, so it is a standard fixture there.

clue.text: Prelude to downing of Guinness entails getting tipsy?

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the word's letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Beginning to knock back the stout means getting a bit drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slainte, Gaelic for health, is the toast said before drinking, as before a pint of Guinness.

clue.text: Wine? One's drunk about a mug

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces wrap round the next

blocks.note: a means one
is lit, lit being slang for drunk
a can is a drinking vessel, a mug

explanation.surface: Wine, anyone? Someone is plastered and holding a tankard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'One's' stands for is, so 'One's drunk' reads as one is lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicant is an old name for the red wine of Alicante in Spain, so it is a kind of wine.

clue.text: Jock's crested tuft, very soft within

indicators.note: something within another sits inside it, so these letters go in the middle

blocks.note: tait, or tate, is a small tuft of hair or wool
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's crest of hair feels very soft inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, signalling a Scots word. TAIT takes PP: TA(PP)IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappit is Scots for crested or topped, as in tappit hen, a hen with a tuft on its head.

clue.text: Cast point of view that may be acute

definitions.text: point of view that may be acute

blocks.note: first meaning: to fish with rod and line

blocks.clueFragment: point of view that may be acute
blocks.note: second meaning: a viewpoint, also the geometric figure that can be acute

explanation.walkthrough: 'acute' in the second definition nods to geometry, where an angle under ninety degrees is acute.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to fish with a line, and as a noun it means an approach or perspective as well as the geometric corner.

clue.text: Nach dancing before king displaying part of girl's adornment

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and take up new places

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An Indian nautch dance before the king shows off a piece of a dancing girl's jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: A nach, or nautch, is an Indian dance performed by professional dancing girls.
explanation.definitionFit: A chank is a conch shell, cut in India into bangles and ornaments, so it forms part of a girl's jewellery.

clue.text: Vehicle, we hear, for one-time star of silver screen

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the spelling may differ from the sound

blocks.note: a lorry is a truck

explanation.surface: A star vehicle was found for an actor of the old cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a film made to showcase a star; it is a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Lorre was a Hungarian-born film actor famous for The Maltese Falcon and Casablanca, a star of classic Hollywood.

clue.text: The inducement that includes love and opening to heaven for believer in karma?

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it within itself
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a sop is something given to pacify or win someone over
the first letter of heaven

explanation.surface: The promise of heaven, mixed with love, tempts someone who believes in fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a zero score in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A theosoph is a theosophist, a follower of a mystical system that teaches karma and reincarnation.

clue.text: Path no longer in use: it is heading west and east

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the words are read right to left

blocks.note: it's, the contraction of it is
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An old track that once went west now goes east too.
explanation.walkthrough: IT'S read westward gives STI, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Stie is an obsolete spelling of sty, an old word for a path or ascent, so it is a path no longer in use.

clue.text: Following rising generation daughter produces swearword (not too offensive)

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the second item follows the first, so it is placed after it

blocks.note: an age is a generation or era
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter trailing the younger generation comes out with a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is a dated, mild oath, a softened form of 'by God', so it is a polite expletive.

clue.text: Pearl oyster has borne? Could be this stone, yes?

indicators.note: could be invites the letters of the longer phrase to be rearranged into the solver's word plus the rest

blocks.note: the fourteen letters of the composite
letters to be taken away from the rearranged fodder

explanation.surface: Has the pearl oyster produced a gem? Could this be the stone?
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus STONE YES rearranges to OYSTER HAS BORNE. Pearl Harbor is the US naval base in Hawaii, spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl Harbor is the Hawaiian naval base, so the answer completes the name that starts with Pearl.

clue.text: Burning green logs, nip one of them in pieces

indicators.note: broken in pieces, the letters can be rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
one of the logs is a single log

explanation.surface: Pinch one of the green logs on the fire and break it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of them' points back to 'logs' in the definition, which serves twice.
explanation.definitionFit: In copper refining, poling is stirring the molten metal with poles of green wood, whose burning gases remove oxygen.

clue.text: Organise RN at sea fit for defence

indicators.note: at sea means confused or adrift, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Get the Royal Navy ready for a defensive operation on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To engarrison is to equip a place with a garrison of troops, readying it to be defended.

clue.text: Something like yoghurt to lift recipe?

blocks.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high into the air
R is the abbreviation for recipe

explanation.surface: A tub of something like yoghurt could brighten up a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyr is an Icelandic cultured dairy product, thick and tangy, very similar to strained yoghurt.

clue.text: Prevent freshwater fish being wiped out (rare)

blocks.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
ged is a northern and Scots name for the pike

explanation.surface: Stopping river fish from being wiped out, since they are rare.
explanation.walkthrough: '(rare)' looks like a note on the endangered fish; it flags the answer as a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deterge is to cleanse or wipe clean, a rarely used verb, so deterged means wiped out.
